Table of contents listing sections and page numbers (Résumé exécutif p.2, Executive summary p.5, Aperçu p.8, Contexte conceptuel p.10, Contexte au Niger p.12, Financement p.18, Plan d'action p.20, Apprentissage p.23, Dispositions finales p.23, Annexe 1 p.24). Main point: cover/TOC for the Niger floods AA framework, approved 24 Oct 2024.

--- page 2 ---
Narrative text (Résumé exécutif - Introduction, Déclencheur intro). Key facts: framework targets riverine (fluvial) flooding of the Niger River; two flood peaks/year — "crue rouge/locale" (July–Sept) and "crue guinéenne" (Nov/Dec–Feb); trigger based on Niger River water level at Niamey station (ABN data) exceeding 580cm. Main point: introduces pilot scope, seasonality, and trigger basis.

FAO $1,000,000 (20%); OIM (IOM) $800,000 (16%); PAM (WFP) $750,000 (15%); UNICEF $550,000 (11%); OMS (WHO) $550,000 (11%); UNFPA $450,000 (9%); UNHCR $450,000 (9%); PNUD (UNDP) $450,000 (9%); Total $5,000,000. Also narrative: trigger is water level >580cm at Niamey (ABN/SATH-ABN); up to $5M CERF available if drought framework window not triggered; 8 UN agencies, 5 sectors. Main point: indicative CERF budget allocation by agency, totaling $5M.

Covers: activities to start immediately once threshold reached, assistance to reach at-risk communities within max 7 days; Apprentissage (learning) section — two learning tracks (agency M&E, potential independent evaluation); Collaboration avec le gouvernement (ABN, DNPGCA/CC-SAP, Ministry of Hydraulics, Direction Météo Nationale); Considérations principales (pilot nature, AA as one tool among many, need for complementary funding — floods recur ~once every 2.7 years).

--- page 5 ---
Narrative text (Executive summary - Introduction, Trigger), English duplicate of pages 2-3 content. Key facts: pilot framework for riverine flooding of Niger River; two flood periods (red/local flood July-Sept; Guinean flood Nov/Dec-Feb); trigger = Niger River water level at Niamey (NBA) exceeds 580cm = "Orange Alert" threshold on SATH-NBA; framework activates only once per season. Main point: English executive summary intro and trigger definition.

Also narrative: Action Plan (8 UN agencies, 5 sectors: food security, health, WASH, shelter/NFI, protection); activities start immediately, reach at-risk communities within 7 days. --- page 10 ---
Diagram: "Réduction de l'impact d'un choc prévisible à travers l'action anticipatoire" — shows two curves comparing "Action Anticipatoire" (starts response earlier, before shock peak, based on forecast/trigger, funding mobilization) vs "Réponse Traditionnelle" (starts after shock, delayed), with the anticipatory path leading to "une réponse humanitaire plus vite, efficace, efficient, et digne." Icons: prévision robuste & cadre de décision, planning and prioritizing, mobilizing & allocating funding. Narrative: pilot objective is to demonstrate collective AA reduces humanitarian impact of floods; combines "trois plus un" components: 1) forecast/trigger model, 2) anticipatory actions, 3) pre-arranged CERF financing, 4) collaborative learning approach.

--- page 11 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Lists "Principes de base" (basic principles) of the pilot: consensus-based work (experts from FAO, WFP, UNDP, UNFPA, WHO, UNICEF, HCR, IOM, Niger Red Cross, Met Direction, Hydraulics Direction, ABN, DNPGCA); multisectoral priority; accountability to affected populations; support to local actors; use of cash transfers where possible; generating development co-benefits; capturing learning; aiming for integration into humanitarian architecture.

--- page 12 ---
Narrative text + start of Table 2. Niger context: arid Sahel country, ~23M population (2021), 48.6% under 15, 2/3 desert, single rainy season June-Oct, rainfall 10mm(north)-800mm(south). Climate change impacts flooding/drought alternation; agriculture >40% GDP. Flood definition: two Niger River flood peaks (red/local flood July-Sept; Guinean flood Nov/Dec-Feb). Table 2 (start): "Echelle standard de classification des seuils d'alertes à la station hydrométrique de Niamey" — Vert: <530cm, <1444 m³/s, situation normale.

--- page 13 ---
Table 2 continued: alert thresholds at Niamey station — Jaune: ≥530 and <580cm, ≥1444 and <1766 m³/s, "risque de crue et montée rapide, vigilance particulière"; Orange: ≥580 and <620cm, ≥1766 and <2046 m³/s, "impacts significatifs possibles sur vie collective et sécurité"; Rouge: ≥620cm, ≥2046 m³/s, "risque de crue majeure, menace directe sur sécurité des personnes et biens". Narrative: 1973-2013 retrospective shows >40 billion CFA francs annual flood losses; ~35,000 households / 200-300k people affected/year on average.

--- page 14 ---
Two bar charts. Figure 1: "Niger, nombre de personnes et de localités affectées par an par les inondations entre 1998 et 2017" — dual axis bar chart (Nombre de personnes 0-700,000 left axis; Nombre de localités 0-1400 right axis) by year 1998-2020, showing rising trend (linear trendlines for both), with major spikes ~2010, 2012, 2020 (person count reaching ~620,000 by 2020, localities ~1200). Figure 2: "Niger, pertes de maisons, cultures et de bétail à cause des inondations par an entre 1998 et 2020" — bar chart (Maisons et UBT left axis 0-60,000; Hectares right axis 0-100,000) by year, showing Pertes de cultures (ha), Pertes d'élevage (UBT), Maisons; largest spikes in 2012 (crop losses ~52,000... scaled, houses ~38,000) and 2020 (houses ~50,000, hectares ~85,000). Text: 1998-2020 total 3,115,290 people and ~7,100 localities affected; >225,000 houses destroyed; ~205,000 ha crop losses; 46,540 UBT (livestock) lost; growth rate >14,000 new people affected/year and 1,100 houses/year.

--- page 15 ---
Map: "REPUBLIQUE DU NIGER — CARTOGRAPHIE DES ZONES A RISQUE D'INONDATION" (MAH/GC, Direction de Prévention et Alerte aux Catastrophes). Shows Niger regions with flood risk shading by "Seuil d'impact population" categories: 0-5.6 (161 communes, lightest), 5.6-11.2 (12), 11.2-16.8 (2), 16.8-22.4 (2), 22.4-28 (1, darkest red) — highest-risk areas concentrated in south/southwest along the Niger River (Dallols), around Arlit/Ingall in north-center, and near Lake Chad in southeast. Fleuve Niger and Lac Tchad marked. Narrative: no region spared, southern band and along Niger River/Dallols/Goulbi/Korama/Komadougou Yobé most affected; 2020-2022 rainfall above 1981-2010 and 1991-2020 averages. Plan Triennal de Contingence Inondations 2023-2025 projections: 2023: 274,657 people/39,236 households sinistrés (-5%); 2024: 247,192 people/35,313 households (-10%); 2025: 222,473 people/31,781 households (-15%), based on 289,112 average people impacted 2016-2021.

--- page 16 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Capacités et lacunes existantes": Capacities — Direction Météorologie Nationale (DMN), DNPGCA, Autorité du Bassin du Niger (ABN, 9 member states: Bénin, Burkina Faso, Cameroun, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinée, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, Tchad); FAO/CRN anticipatory pilots in 2023 (Djirataoua, Safo, Madarounfa in Maradi; Diffa, Gueskerou in Diffa). Lacunes (gaps): reactive-dominant management, fragmented institutional framework, weak sub-national capacities, rigid financing mechanisms, weak DRR/climate adaptation integration, underuse of traditional/local knowledge.

--- page 17 ---
Map (Figure 3): "Carte du fleuve Niger" — West/Central Africa map showing the Niger River basin (blue shaded watershed) spanning Guinea, Mali, Burkina Faso, Benin, Niger, Nigeria, Cameroon; Niamey marked on the river. Line chart: "Station: Niamey" water level (cm) June 2023-May 2024, y-axis 0-650cm with color bands (grey <~100 normal-low, green ~100-530 normal, yellow ~530-580, orange/pink ~580-620, red ≥620); blue line shows level rising from ~150cm (June) to peak ~560cm (~Sept-Oct), staying ~500-550cm through Jan-Feb, declining to ~170cm by May. Purple horizontal line marks trigger at 580cm — level in this example year stayed below trigger (in yellow zone, peaking just under 580). Text: trigger = 580cm at Niamey = "Alerte orange"; single activation per season (red flood July-Sept or Guinean flood Nov-Feb); return period ~3 (2.7) years based on 2005-2024 data (would have triggered 7 of 19 seasons).

--- page 18 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Trigger history: threshold reached in 7 years for local floods (2012,2013,2016,2017,2018,2019,2020 — always early Aug to mid-Sept) vs 2 years for Guinean floods (2019, 2021 — always early January); ~7 days between trigger and maximum flood extent at Gaya department (downstream). Protocole de suivi et activation: 4-step process (CHD alerts Coordinatrice/OCHA/CERF/agencies; CERF secretariat initiates disbursement; OCHA convenes ad hoc meeting; agencies implement upon CERF approval letters). CERF section: created 2005 by UN General Assembly resolution A/RES/60/124, objectives include promoting early action, improving response to urgent needs, strengthening underfunded crisis response, life-saving priority assistance.

--- page 19 ---
Table (repeat of Table 1): Agence/CERF — FAO $1,000,000; OIM $800,000; PAM $750,000; UNICEF $550,000; OMS $550,000; UNFPA $450,000; UNHCR $450,000; PNUD $450,000; Total $5,000,000. Narrative: CERF pre-arranges up to $5M for Niger flood AA if triggers met, disbursed once 3 conditions met (HC/RC approval of framework+CERF submission; ERC approval; trigger activation within max 2 years of ERC framework approval). Combined CERF ceiling for drought+flood AA frameworks capped at $15M — flood framework only funded if drought window not activated. Framework activates max once per season. FAO has separate SFERA special fund (~$1M for 2024/2025 seasons) for early action.

--- page 20 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Autres bailleurs de fonds": other funding instruments mentioned (World Bank Crisis Response Window/CRW, Education Cannot Wait/ECW, bilateral donors, UN agency reserve funds). "Plan d'action anticipatoire — Critères de sélection": 6 selection criteria for anticipatory actions: caractère anticipatoire, capacité à livrer dans la fenêtre d'opportunité (~7-10 days), capacité opérationnelle, approche sans regret, bénéfice d'approche multisectorielle, effet multiplicateur. Start of "Actions sélectionnées" — Générale: alert message diffusion, unconditional cash transfers.

--- page 21 ---
Narrative text, no figure. Detailed list of sector-specific anticipatory actions: Abris et Biens Non-Alimentaires (ABNA) — emergency/repair kits, NFI kits, evacuation of vulnerable people + management of evacuation centers (max 10 days); Sécurité Alimentaire & Moyens d'existence — storage/protection tools, cash transfers, livestock health support; Santé — health worker coaching, cash transfers for emergency obstetric care + hygiene products, sexual/reproductive health kits, medical stock provisioning (incl. cholera prevention); Eau, Hygiène et Assainissement (EHA) — dignity/menstrual hygiene kits, hygiene promotion, emergency latrines + safe water storage, cash-for-work canal clearing; Protection — community sensitization on GBV/child protection.

--- page 22 ---
Table 3: "Communes Ciblées" — 6 priority communes selected via 2-step process (identification of 31 communes in Tillabéri/Dosso along river; prioritization by access, partner capacity, expert judgment). Rows: 1) Dosso/Gaya/Gaya - vulnerability "Faiblement", access accessible/accessible, score 3, pop 99,362; 2) Dosso/Gaya/Tanda - accessible/difficultés, score 2, pop 77,810; 3) Dosso/Gaya/Tounouga - accessible/difficultés, score 2, pop 66,713; 4) Tillaberi/Kollo/Karma - accessible/accessible, score 3, pop 136,195; 5) Tillaberi/Kollo/N'Dounga - accessible/accessible, score 3, pop 34,487; 6) Tillaberi/Kollo/Liboré - accessible/accessible, score 3, pop 40,513. Total population 455,080. Main point: 6 targeted communes (Gaya, Tanda, Tounouga in Dosso; Karma, N'Dounga, Liboré in Tillabéri) totaling ~455,080 people.

--- page 23 ---
Narrative text, no figure. "Apprentissage": ad hoc learning/M&E committee convened by OCHA; S&E section — post-distribution monitoring (PDM) by agencies with DNPGCA/DMN; common questions on impact on survival/quality of life, timing effectiveness, comparison to past post-disaster response, multiplier effects. "Potentielle évaluation indépendante": possible final independent evaluation. "Dispositions finales — Plaidoyer et communication publique": joint press release and coordinated messaging upon activation.

--- page 24 ---
Line/step chart: "Niamey période de retour (depuis 2005)" — water level (cm, y-axis 450-600+) vs return period (years, x-axis 1-10), step function showing: 1.5-ans = 492cm, 2-ans = 520cm, 3-ans = 582cm, 5-ans = 612cm. Narrative: trigger (580cm, ~3-year/2.7-year return period) based on 2005-2023 ABN data validated by CHD. Local flood trigger dates reached: 19 Aug 2012, 30 Aug 2013, 13 Sept 2016, 7 Sept 2017, 25 Aug 2018, 27 Aug 2019, 8 Aug 2020. Guinean flood trigger dates: 3 Jan 2019 (2018 season), 12 Jan 2021 (2020 season).

--- page 25 ---
Two figures. Scatter plot: "Comparaison d'impact et niveau d'eau (2010-2020)" — x-axis Niveau d'eau à Niamey maximum (cm) 525-700, y-axis Maisons détruites total across target communes 0-6000; quadrants labeled Faux négatif/Vrai positif/Vrai négatif/Faux positif split by trigger threshold (580cm vertical) and impact return-period threshold (~1300 houses, horizontal). Points labeled by year: 2018 (~590cm, ~5800 houses, vrai positif/highest), 2012 (~605cm, ~4400), 2013 (~600cm, ~2900), 2017 (~595cm, ~2200), 2015 (~578cm, ~1050, borderline, "très proche mais n'aurait pas activé"), 2010 (~565cm, low), 2011 (~535cm, ~0), 2016 (~595cm, low, faux positif), 2019 (~625cm, low), 2020 (~700cm, ~0 in these communes despite highest water level — noted "beaucoup d'autre part"). Second figure: "Inondations depuis 1998 à Dosso et Tillabéri" (Floodscan) — flood extent fraction vs day of season (since June 1) for Gaya, Tounouga, Tanda communes, showing peak flooded fraction (~0.035-0.04) around day 50-150 (roughly July-Oct), Gaya highest peak, small secondary bumps ~day 250-360.

--- page 26 ---
Six scatter plots with correlation values. Top row: "Étendue d'inondation" vs "Niveau d'eau maximum (cm)" for Gaya (Corrélation=0.72), Tounouga (Corrélation=0.50), Tanda (Corrélation=0.64) — all show positive trend lines. Bottom row: "Maisons détruites" vs "Étendue d'inondation" for Gaya (Corrélation=0.80), Tounouga (Corrélation=0.74), Tanda (Corrélation=0.63) — positive trend lines. Main point: moderate-to-strong positive correlations support using Niamey water level as flood predictor and Floodscan extent as impact proxy. Text: "Préavis" section — using 2020 example, 580cm threshold reached 8 Aug, max flood extent reached 18 Aug = 10-day lead time; average lead time across triggering years (2012,2013,2016,2017,2018,2019,2020) = 7 days.

--- page 27 ---
Dual-axis line chart: "Inondations à Gaya, Tounouga, et Tanda en 2020" — Niveau d'eau à Niamey (cm, blue line, left axis 0-800) and Étendue d'inondation (red line, right axis 0-0.002) from Jul 2020 to Jan 2021. Vertical dashed lines mark "Déclenchement: Aug 08" (trigger date, blue line crosses ~580-600cm) and "Etendue max.: Aug 18 (préavis 10 jours)" (flood extent peak, red line highest ~0.0018-0.002). Water level peaks ~700cm around late Aug, stays elevated (~500-600cm) through year-end. End of document ("Fin du document").
